description: Attempt to bypass request-object signature validation by sending an unsigned (alg=none) request object and see if the authorization endpoint accepts and processes it.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must not accept an unsigned OIDC request object (alg=none) in a way that influences consumed authorization parameters; it should be rejected or treated as unsupported.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Authorization endpoint accepted an unsigned request object (alg=none) and may have processed attacker-controlled parameters, violating proof integrity.

description: Try to exchange a subject_token while lying about which upstream connector should verify it (connector_id substitution).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control token exchange failed; cannot attribute any rejection/acceptance in the attack path to proof-integrity enforcement.

description: Attempt to inject an unsigned JWT via id_token_hint to influence the consumed identity/claims without proper signature verification.

description: Brokered-flow attack: attempt token exchange using a subject_token that should not validate under the configured OIDC connector trust anchor (issuer/JWKS substitution). Includes a control exchange attempt for baseline behavior.

Dex accepted a subject_token that should not validate under the configured connector trust anchor (issuer/JWKS substitution), indicating proof integrity failure.

description: Brokered-flow attack: attempt token exchange with a JWT that uses attacker-controlled kid/header to try to select a malicious key (kid injection / untrusted key). Includes a control exchange using a known-good upstream token.

description: Direct endpoint attack: attempt to smuggle/override semantic authorization parameters via an unsigned request object (alg=none), focusing on state/nonce coherence inside the consumed request vs what was verified.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted an unsigned (alg=none) request object; if processed, this breaks proof integrity by allowing attacker-controlled authorization semantics without authenticity.

description: Authorization code replay: redeem the same auth code twice and ensure the second redemption is rejected (one-time code anti-replay). Includes two browser sessions (two states) to satisfy multi-identity/session requirement.
